sections.h2: Who handles what at Pitt County Tax Administration
sections.html:
Tax Administration in Greenville lists, appraises and assesses property, and it also collects current and delinquent taxes. Appeals mail goes to PO Box 43, Greenville, NC 27835-0043, and the phone number is 252-902-3400.

Work is split by division. Real Property takes builder exemption forms, Business Personal Property covers farm equipment and similar items, and a Tax Relief Division receives applications for exclusions and deferrals. The county posts an email address for relief questions.

  • Appeals: the formal appeal form and the clerk to the county appeals board.
  • Relief: the Tax Relief Division, or the assessor by mail.
  • Billing and payment methods: Tax Administration.

Ask which jurisdictions tax a given parcel, since a house inside a town may carry more than one bill.

The county has 86,063 housing units and 74,533 households. Owners occupy 51.4% of homes, so renting is nearly as common as owning, and the middle owner home is worth $208,900. The estimated population is 182,936, up 6.5% from the 2020 base.

Ask the tax office how a change of ownership affects any relief or present-use file on a parcel before you list.

The current schedule of values took effect January 1, 2024 and runs until the next revaluation, set for 2028. Improvements made in between are priced under the same statutory standards.

The schedule is a manual of rates, value ranges and guidelines that commissioners must adopt. It covers construction adjustments, market adjustments and land schedules. The Machinery Act defines market value as what a willing and able buyer and seller would agree on without pressure and with reasonable knowledge of the property's uses.

State law (G.S. 105-286) also calls for a review in the fourth year after a reappraisal, using percentage adjustments by category or area instead of appraising each parcel. Ask the assessor whether one is planned before 2028.

Submit a formal appeal form to the county board. Appeals can be filed from January 1 until the board formally adjourns, usually in April or May.

The board is made up of residents chosen by the commissioners and serves as the first step of review. It hears from the owner and from the assessor's office. There are three grounds: a value above market, unequal treatment against similar properties, and factual errors in the record.

Hearings are held at the Eugene James Auditorium, second floor, Pitt County Administration Building, 1717 W. 5th St., Greenville. The request deadline and hearing dates shift each year, so read the current notice, and note that anything filed after adjournment is untimely.

Bring comparable sales, an appraisal if you have one, and photos of the house. You may speak yourself or send a representative.

If you dislike the ruling, you can go to the statewide Property Tax Commission with a written notice filed a month after the ruling is mailed, copied to the assessor (G.S. 105-290).

Relief covers seniors, disabled owners, veterans, farmland, builders, nonprofits and vehicle owners. The homestead programs require that you own the home and live in it.

Pitt County homestead relief for 2027, based on 2026 income
ProgramBenefitIncome limit
Age-or-disability exclusionSubtracts $25,000 or 50% of the home's value, whichever is larger, from the house and up to one acre$39,900
Circuit breakerTax limited to 4% of income at or under $39,900 and 5% from $39,901 to $59,850; the remainder is deferred as a lien$59,850
Disabled veteran exclusion$45,000 off the value for a 100% permanent service-connected disability, or an unmarried surviving spouseNone

File Form AV-9 with the assessor from January 1 through June 1. Late requests from June 2 through December 31 can be considered when you document a reason, and they go to the appeals board. Nothing filed after December 31 can be taken for that year. The circuit breaker is renewed every year, and every owner on the deed has to qualify. Deferred tax, up to three years plus interest, is payable on a sale or a death.

Land in the present-use program carries its own rules: 10 acres for agriculture, 5 for horticulture and 20 for forestry under a written plan. Removal brings rollback of the current and prior three years.

sections.h2: Other exemptions that can touch a sale
sections.html:
Several exemptions matter when the property is not an ordinary house. Each has its own form and timing.

  • Builder inventory: a residential builder's gains from subdividing, grading or building a new single-family home or duplex are excluded for up to three years after first listing, and a commercial builder's for up to five, ending sooner at a building permit or a sale. The form is AV-65.
  • Nonprofit and special-use property: the AV-10 application goes to the Tax Relief Division during January of the year you apply.
  • Antique automobiles: a vehicle that meets the county's conditions is valued at $500, with the application due a month after the tax due date.
  • Antique airplanes: assessed at the lower of true value or $5,000.

A sale ends the builder exclusion, so confirm with the Real Property Division how the end date is handled on a particular parcel, and whether the new owner must file a fresh application.

sections.h2: What you owe at a Pitt County closing
sections.html:
Real property tax is due September 1, interest-free through January 5, with interest starting after that (G.S. 105-360). A same-day postmark now requires a visit to a Postal Service retail counter, so do not count on a late drop in the mail.

The year's lien follows the land (G.S. 105-355). Your closing attorney requests a payoff and takes it from your proceeds.

  • Get a payoff for each parcel and taxing jurisdiction.
  • Check present-use or circuit breaker deferrals, which can come due.
  • Confirm any late relief application was decided.

A cash buyer can close quickly, so request the payoff early. Keep the paid receipts in your closing file in case a question comes up later.

faqs.q: When will Pitt County revalue next?
faqs.a: The current schedule of values holds until the next revaluation in 2028. Confirm the date with Tax Administration.

faqs.q: How do I challenge an assessment?
faqs.a: File the formal appeal form with the county appeals board any time from January 1 until it adjourns, typically April or May. The clerk's number is 252-902-3400.

faqs.q: What is the senior exclusion income cap?
faqs.a: $39,900 for 2027, based on 2026 income, for residents who are 65 or over, or totally and permanently disabled, and live in the home.

faqs.q: Is a filing after June 1 hopeless?
faqs.a: Not always. Requests from June 2 to December 31 may be reviewed by the appeals board when you give a documented reason, but nothing after December 31 counts for that year.

faqs.q: What happens to deferred tax if I sell?
faqs.a: Circuit breaker deferrals for up to three years plus interest become payable on a sale, and present-use land owes rollback taxes if it leaves the program.
